 Cedrick Frazier claims victory as Hennepin County Attorney
 By KSTP 
 --> 
 PIctured: Cedrick Frazier (Left) and Anders Folk (Right)
 UPDATE: Cedrick Frazier claims victory on the race for Hennepin County Attorney against Anders Folk. 
 As of 11:30 pm., less than 1% of the race has not been called, but Frazier is leading by more than 8,000 votes. 
 Frazier will become the state’s first-ever African American County Attorney in its 168-year history, according to his campaign. 
 Read Frazier’s full statement below: 
 “This was a grassroots campaign powered by working-class people across this county. Since launching last August, we knocked on more than 200,000 doors, showed up at community events, held three public town hall meetings on gun violence, and met people where they were. We listened to peoples’ concerns, learned from their experiences, and built a countywide working-class coalition. 
 This victory is a mandate, and the people have sent a crystal clear message: we need forward-looking change, and we will not return to a failed status quo. The people have demanded a better approach, and we have a responsibility to deliver that. 
 Tonight, as the campaign ends, the real work begins. As your next County Attorney, I understand the responsibility that comes with leading this office. I will work every single day to uphold equal justice and strengthen public safety.” 
 With Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty deciding not to seek reelection, residents will choose between candidates Anders Folk and Cedrick Frazier.
 The office has come into the public focus a lot recently, largely due to Operation Metro Surge, youth gang violence and criticism over some prosecutorial decisions. How will that change with a new person leading the office?
 RELATED: Hennepin County attorney candidates lay out priorities ahead of November election 
 Anders Folk
 A newcomer to politics, the Hennepin County Attorney’s race is Folk’s first time running in an election. 
 Folk grew up in Hopkins, attended Hopkins High School, and later earned a law degree at the University of Minnesota. During law school, Anders worked in the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office under Amy Klobuchar, who was then acting County Attorney. 
 RELATED: How to get November election results and watch coverage 
 After law school, Folk joined the Marine Corps, earning his commission after his second year in law school and entering active duty service after the terrorist attack on Sept. 11.
 Folk then became a federal prosecutor, later signing the federal indictment that charged former Minneapolis Police Officer Derek Chauvin with violating George Floyd’s civil rights.
 Courtesy: Folk for Hennepin County Attorney According to Folk’s election website , if elected, he plans to prioritize charges against repeat and violent offenders, build and strengthen law enforcement partnerships, foster safe communities to reduce crime, and establish clear safeguards for how the Attorney’s Office uses technology and AI, among other priorities .
 Folk describes himself as a Democrat and has endorsements from several local Hennepin County officials, including Mayor Jacob Frey and Hennepin County Sheriff Dawanna Witt.
 Cedrick Frazier
 Frazier currently serves in the Minnesota House of Representatives, representing District 43A.
 Frazier said he grew up on the South Side of Chicago, a place he said faced many hardships, including gang violence, drug trafficking and an ineffective justice system.
 After coming to Minnesota to attend college and play football, Frazier stayed in the state to attend law school and became a public defender in Hennepin County. 
 Frazier later became legal counsel for Minneapolis Public Schools, a labor attorney representing educators across Minnesota, and the first African American to serve on the New Hop City Council in 2018.
 In 2020, Frazier was elected to the Minnesota House of Representatives for District 45A. In 2024, Frazier won another election, this time for District 43A.
 Courtesy: Cedrick Frazier Among Frazier’s priorities, according to his campaign website, is prosecuting federal agents who violated Minnesota law; the website also states that, if elected, the Hennepin County Attorney’s Office would “never work with ICE.” Other priorities listed include confronting fentanyl trafficking, disrupting gun violence, and combating wage theft.
 Frazier is endorsed by the DFL, Lt. Governor and U.S. Senate candidate Peggy Flanagan, Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison and U.S. Congresswoman Ilhan Omar.
